narrative:
The system estimates there’s a 57% chance you’ll leave your job in the near future—well above the 40% threshold we use to assess promotion readiness. Because of this, the promotion was denied.

The prediction is driven by three key factors. First, you’ve received other job offers while working here, which strongly suggests you’re actively exploring opportunities elsewhere. Second, your total work experience is still on the lower side, which typically makes employees more likely to stay, but in your case, this effect was outweighed by other concerns. Finally, you’ve spent several years in your current role without advancing, which may be contributing to your restlessness.

Other details reinforce this picture. You’ve never attended training programs, and you don’t feel they’d be useful—yet most promoted employees have participated in at least some development. You’re also dissatisfied with your wages and don’t believe you’ve received the promotions you deserve, which is uncommon among those who’ve been promoted. While you feel recognized and emotionally committed to the company, these positives weren’t enough to offset the risk factors.

To improve your chances next time, focus on two things: deepening your roots here and addressing your concerns. Discuss clear career progression with your manager, request meaningful training, and explore whether adjustments to your role or compensation could make staying more appealing. If you’re no longer actively pursuing other jobs, that shift alone would significantly lower the predicted risk.
